plainTitle: Church Street closed to cars for a summer 2026 pilot

whatIsProposed.text: City Council allowed Church Street to be closed to cars between Wellesley Street East and Alexander Street from June 19 to August 21, 2026, for a street event called the Church Street Pedestrianization Plan / Village Fest.

citations.quote: requiring the closure of Church Street to vehicular traffic, between Wellesley Street East and Alexander Street, but not including east-west intersections, from June 19, 2026 to August 21, 2026, inclusive

whatIsProposed.text: The cross streets that run east-west stay open to traffic. Only Church Street itself is closed.

citations.quote: leaving all east-west corridors open to vehicular traffic

whatIsProposed.text: The City also waived its application and permit fees for the Church-Wellesley Business Improvement Area for this street event.

citations.quote: City Council direct the General Manager, Transportation Services to waive the application and permit fees charged in relation to any application by the Church-Wellesley Business Improvement Area

why.text: The councillor's letter says closing the street to cars improves road safety and accessibility and brings in more business.

citations.quote: Pedestrianization significantly enhances urban quality of life by improving road safety, increasing accessibility, and driving sustained commercial activity.

why.text: The letter says this stretch has no bus or streetcar route, so closing it would cause little disruption to the TTC.

citations.quote: due to the absence of dedicated bus or streetcar routes, ensuring minimal disruption to the TTC’s broader network

why.text: The pilot is also meant to help the City write a policy on closing streets to cars, for the summer or for good.

citations.quote: to help inform the creation of a pedestrianization policy and identification of resource requirements for seasonal and permanent arterial roadway closures

whoIsAffected.text: People who drive, park or make deliveries on Church Street between Wellesley Street East and Alexander Street during the closure.

citations.quote: the closure of Church Street to vehicular traffic, between Wellesley Street East and Alexander Street

whoIsAffected.text: People who use Wheel-Trans: the letter says there would be pick-up and drop-off zones for Wheel-Trans and extra ramps.

citations.quote: including dedicated pick-up and drop-off zones for WheelTrans and installing additional ramps at regular intervals

whoIsAffected.text: Businesses, residents and visitors in the Church-Wellesley Village. The City lists one ward for this item: 13 (Toronto Centre).

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: The closure comes with whatever conditions the head of Transportation Services and the City Solicitor think are appropriate.

citations.quote: with such conditions deemed appropriate in the opinion of the General Manager, Transportation Services and the City Solicitor

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: City Council added a rule that Transportation Services can cancel the closure if there are serious problems, such as public safety risks, slower emergency response, traffic problems, or if permit conditions are not followed.

citations.quote: cancel the temporary closure of Church Street on the basis of unacceptable impacts or concerns related to public safety or security, emergency service response times, traffic-related operational concerns, or non-compliance with any conditions attached to the permit authorizing the closure

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: City staff are asked to evaluate the closure afterward, looking at community participation, road safety, social and economic benefits, and risks.
conditionsAndUnknowns.caveat: The record does not give a date for that evaluation or say who it will be reported to.

citations.quote: to evaluate outcomes of the temporary closure of Church Street, including levels of community participation and engagement, improvements in road safety, and overall social and economic benefits, alongside risks and public safety impacts

committee.text: Toronto and East York Community Council recommended the closure, the evaluation and the fee waiver. The vote was 6 to 0.

citations.quote: Toronto and East York Community Council recommends that:

council.text: City Council approved the pilot and added the power to cancel the closure if problems arise. The amendment passed 16 to 8, and the final item passed 20 to 4.

citations.quote: City Council adopted this item on May 20 and 21, 2026 with amendments.

whatHappensNext.text: The closure was set for June 19 to August 21, 2026. After it, staff are to evaluate the results to help shape a future City policy on closing streets to cars.
whatHappensNext.caveat: The record does not show whether the closure went ahead as planned or what the evaluation found.

citations.quote: for the period June 19 to August 21, 2026
to help inform the creation of a pedestrianization policy
